name: rare-claim-reachable

finding.title: `refresh()` can store a new socket on a closed session and leak it
finding.description: `refresh()` checks `self._closed` and then opens a new socket without taking `self._lock`. When `close()` runs between the check and the assignment, the new socket is stored on a closed session and nothing closes it. The docstring this PR adds tells users to call `refresh()` from a background thread while the main thread keeps using the session, so `refresh()` and `close()` run at the same time in normal use.
finding.suggestedFix: Hold `self._lock` across the check and the assignment in `refresh()`.

prDiff:
diff --git a/sdk/session.py b/sdk/session.py
index 1111111..2222222 100644
--- a/sdk/session.py
+++ b/sdk/session.py
@@ -20,7 +20,19 @@ class Session:
         self._sock = _connect(self._host)
         self._closed = False
 
+    def refresh(self):
+        """Reconnect with a fresh token.
+
+        Tokens expire after an hour. Call this from a background thread
+        every few minutes while the main thread keeps using the session.
+        """
+        if self._closed:
+            return
+        old = self._sock
+        self._sock = _connect(self._host)
+        old.close()
+
     def close(self):
         with self._lock:
             self._closed = True
             self._sock.close()
